- We can support the routing policy you outlined (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with one caveat: for the 32k token flows we recommend using a quantized dedicated/private variant to keep latency predictable under load.
- KV caching: Redwood's prefix/KV cache is per-model + per-customer namespace. For 32k flows we'd suggest a short TTL (30s–2m) for conversational prefixes used in retrieval-augmented generation; for full-session caching we recommend pinning to dedicated capacity.
- Smoke test checklist: I'll attach a short POC checklist (redwood_poc_checklist.md) with minimum telemetry hooks we need (token breakdown, per-route latency p50/p95, outlier failure traces).

Sergio — can you take point on kernel/quantization notes and draft a brief of any binary compatibility checks we should add to PulseForge's matrix? Aditya — can you validate the proposed latency baseline numbers with current dedicated profiles in eu-west?

On Mon, 17 Aug 2026 at 10:08, kimberly.park@redwood.com wrote:
> Elena / Ravi — thanks for the docs and the clear matrix. Quick confirmation and next steps from our side:
>
> - We can support the routing policy you outlined (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with one caveat: for the 32k token flows we recommend using a quantized dedicated/private variant to keep latency predictable under load.

Notes and suggested checklist items (technical):

1) Kernel / quantization compatibility
   - PulseForge SDK uses FP16 by default. For 32k-token long-contexts we recommend the partner test both FP16 and 8-bit quantized variants; our runtime will expose small differences in latency and memory use.

2) KV cache validation
   - Confirm that PulseForge's session IDs are preserved across retries; our cache key scheme is model_id + customer_namespace + session_id + prefix_hash. If session_id changes on the client side each request, cache hit-rate will be near zero. Suggest adding a simple header in the matrix to indicate session id behavior.

3) Batching behavior & SLOs
   - For the POC, set a baseline of p50 <= 150ms for short-turn prompts (<=512 tokens) on dedicated eu-west GPU pool. p95 targets will depend on batching; include both single-request and batched scenarios in the matrix.

4) Failure modes and fallbacks
   - Add tests for model-fallback behavior: deliberate model OOM on hosted -> measure failover time to dedicated and ensure no more than 3s increased tail latency. Also test region-fallback when eu-west capacity exhausted (route to eu-central).

5) Telemetry hooks we need from PulseForge
   - request_id, session_id, token_counts, model_variant, region, and client-side timing for submit->receive.

I'll update the integration_test_matrix.xlsx with the above rows and re-upload. Once we have those in place we can run an automated smoke sweep (scripted in our lab).

—Sergio
